chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ya'qub al-Hashimi, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"When the sun and the moon eclipse, and the entire [disk] is eclipsed, it is incumbent upon the people to hasten to an Imam so that he may lead them in prayer. And whichever of them [the sun or moon] is partially eclipsed, it is sufficient for a man to pray alone. The prayer of the eclipse consists of ten bowings (ruku') and four prostrations (sajdahs). The eclipse of the sun is more severe for the people and the animals."

key_terms.الْكُسُوفُ: Eclipse (specifically of the sun or moon)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific number of bowings and prostrations in the Islamic eclipse prayer, and when is it performed individually versus congregationally?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the specific ritual structure of the eclipse prayer, distinguishing between the communal obligation (fard kifaya) during a total eclipse and the individual sufficiency for partial eclipses. It highlights the unique prostration-based format of ten bowings and four prostrations, reflecting the Shia juristic tradition that emphasizes the awe-inspiring nature of celestial signs as reminders of divine power.
